summary: This attempt closes O-026 and O-027 and changes no src (src is identical to the attempt-1 commit). O-026: the shared path-API name list now also holds GetCompressedFileSize[AW]?, FindFirstFileName[AW]?, FindFirstStream[AW]?, GetFileInformationByName and CreateFileTransacted[AW]?. It is updated in both yaml patterns and both ArchitectureRulesTests patterns. The texts now say the rule holds only the entry points it names; they no longer claim every path-taking call. O-027: the Kernel32 count Fact no longer has a copy of its own. It reads the two patterns out of PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen's source, the same copy rules-parity compares with the yaml. I planted GetCompressedFileSizeW in Kernel32.cs and the count Fact failed on it; that name exists only in the twin Fact's source. On the merged tree (uat with SL-076): rules-parity AGREE at 29 patterns under both shells, all 14 RuleCases cases held, the harness shows 56 of 56 AS-RECORDED, SL-076's bug test held, the full suite passed 414 of 414, and the repro command exits 0. The published exe on the empty E:\ still ends RootUnreadable/21 with child error mode 0x0 and no box.

files.why: PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen: both must_not_match patterns gain the five names from review m1. The `because` now says 'the named path-taking entry points', and that a call by a name missing from the list passes the rule. It also says the Kernel32 count uses this rule's own patterns.

The twin Fact's two verbatim patterns gain the same five names, so rules-parity still reads AGREE at 29 patterns. The doc comment gets the same scope wording, and says FailCriticalErrorsTests reads these two patterns from this source.

Kernel32MakesOnlyThePathCallsThatRunInsideTheScope drops its `const string names` copy. A new helper, FactPatterns, reads PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen's pattern lines from ArchitectureRulesTests.cs the way rules-parity reads them (one verbatim literal per line, ending ',' or ');'). It unescapes the doubled quotes and compiles with Multiline. The Fact asserts that there are exactly two patterns, each with group 1. Its doc no longer promises that any other path call is counted.

obligations.how: I added GetCompressedFileSize[AW]?, FindFirstFileName[AW]?, FindFirstStream[AW]?, GetFileInformationByName and CreateFileTransacted[AW]? to the name list in both yaml patterns and both ArchitectureRulesTests patterns. The count Fact now reads those patterns, so it picks them up too. Checked with .NET Regex (Multiline) on the six inputs the review named: Win.GetCompressedFileSizeW(, the EntryPoint = "GetCompressedFileSizeW" import, FindFirstFileNameW(, FindFirstStreamW(, GetFileInformationByName( and CreateFileTransactedW( all fire now, each capturing the full name as group 1. The CreateFileW controls still fire, and GetFileInformationByHandleEx, GetVolumeInformationByHandle and "GetVolumeInformationByHandleW" stay quiet. src has no hits outside the two excepted files. I reworded 'every path-taking entry point' in fitness.yaml to 'the named path-taking entry points', with a sentence that an unlisted name passes. The count Fact's 'Any other path call or path import' now reads 'a call or import of any other named entry point', and it says an unlisted name is not counted. rules-parity: AGREE 12 facts from 16 twinned entries, 29 patterns (unchanged), exit 0 under pwsh and powershell.exe. Harness: 56 rows, 56 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0.

I dropped the third literal. The count Fact takes its patterns from ArchitectureRulesTests.cs's PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen source (FactPatterns, which finds the Fact through nameof and reads its verbatim pattern lines as rules-parity does). It fails if that Fact stops having exactly two patterns with the name in group 1. Proof it follows the rule: I planted `private const string PlantedPathCall = "GetCompressedFileSizeW";` in Kernel32.cs and the count Fact failed, listing 'GetCompressedFileSizeW: private const string PlantedPathCall = ...'. That name is only in the twin Fact's source, not in any literal the count Fact holds. Kernel32.cs was restored with an identical SHA-256.

cases.test_name: FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.LinkTests, HardlinkTests, OnDiskSizeTests, LongPathTests, UnreadableFolderTests (counting-rule suite, unchanged)

deviations: None from the design. For O-027 I took the stronger of the two options the disposition offered: the count Fact reads the twin Fact's patterns from source, rather than keeping its own literal and asserting that it appears in them. It then holds no copy of the name list at all.
not_built: No plants.json row for the five new names. The finding asked only for the name list, the rewording and re-runs of parity and the harness. F26 already proves the entry-point-string form fires in both engines, and the new names go through the same two patterns.

Carried over, unchanged: no opt-in empty-drive Fact (the M1 disposition said not to add one); handle-based calls after media removal are still out of scope (C-014, open question); no regex ban on `new`/`default` CriticalErrorBoxOff (the disposition judged it unreliable).

follow_ups: This rule has been widened on every review lap: m2, then R2-m2, now m1. A name list can always be one entry short, and the texts now say so. The closing answer is behavioural: the process-wide SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS) at App startup (review m1 of the first critique, deferred to the handle-based-calls follow-up) covers any entry point, named or not. If a fourth widening is asked for, a person should first decide whether that slice is the better place for it.

Nobody has measured that the empty-drive check can fail. Running the pre-fix exe (uat 14acea3) with -DefaultErrorMode on E:\ would show it, but it puts a modal 'insert a disk' box on the person's screen, so it needs a person present.

The design record still has would_force_resynthesis: true on the per-open cost question (measured at about 37 ns against 15.8 µs per open). Its key_decision rejecting a process-wide call should be restated on the grounds in m1's disposition.
At merge, check that the engine does not re-add a '# settled by SL-077' block under the design's prose rule name. It would duplicate the twinned entry (HF-008).
